status: exact hard-wall normal-mode witness; bottom-up model input rather than a four-dimensional Yang-Mills construction

hardWall.bulk: AdS5 scalar dual to the dimension-four operator Tr F^2

sensitivity.meaning: the gap is proportional to the imposed infrared wall scale

positive: a confining radial boundary produces a discrete gauge-invariant scalar spectrum
dimensionless mass ratios follow from the Sturm-Liouville problem once boundary conditions are chosen
the construction is a useful spectral ansatz and comparison target
missing: derivation of the five-dimensional background and wall from the four-dimensional Yang-Mills measure
proof of holographic duality for finite-N pure four-dimensional Yang-Mills
Osterwalder-Schrader construction and regulator-independent R4 continuum limit
removal of Kaluza-Klein and other extra states in top-down confining backgrounds
prediction of z0 from the Spin(2,3) scale rather than identification by hand

spin23Boundary.bulkGroupMismatch: AdS5 uses SO(2,4), whereas Spin(2,3) is the AdS4 group
spin23Boundary.allowedUse: Spin(2,3) may motivate an AdS4 gravitational phase, but a 3+1-dimensional Yang-Mills holographic dual requires an additional radial organization and normally an AdS5-like parent
spin23Boundary.nonPromotion: a discrete bulk normal-mode spectrum is not a proof of the boundary Yang-Mills theory unless the duality and boundary theory are constructed

decision: Holographic confinement can generate an explicit discrete gap and robust ratios, but the hard-wall scale and dual background are extra inputs. Spin(2,3) alone is dimensionally the wrong AdS group for a direct 4D boundary dual, so this route remains a calculational laboratory rather than the Clay construction.
